title: Crafting Your Own Story Adventure
welcome_lead: Now you'll apply the toolkit — building atmosphere and structuring a narrative.
meta_desc: GCSE English Language narrative writing — structure, openings, in medias res, varied sentences.
final_note: You practised building atmospheric openings, using structural devices and varying your sentences.

concepts.def: Starting a story in the middle of the action
Jumping back to an earlier event
Mixing short and long for pace and impact
A grammatically incomplete sentence for effect. Like this.
An unresolved ending that hooks the reader

walkthroughs.body_html:
Hook the reader fast with in medias res — drop us into the action.

Example: 'The brakes screamed. Too late.'

Long sentences slow the reader down — perfect for setting a scene.

Short ones punch. They speed things up. They jolt.
Try a cyclical structure: open and close on the same image — a key in a lock, a single feather — for a satisfying echo.

mcqs.q: A story that opens with 'The bullet missed by inches' uses what structural device?
Which sentence creates the most dramatic pace?
options: He walked slowly down the long, winding corridor.
He ran. He stopped. He listened.
He noticed the door was slightly open.
He decided he would go upstairs eventually.

numericals.q: A 'cyclical' structure has how many matching points (start and end)?
numericals.hint: It's a circle — beginning and end.
